blocks.content: This topic goes past the Architecture module's overview into the full, precise pipeline every request travels through, including a real, specific detail: admission control actually runs in two distinct sub-phases.

Every request travels through, in strict order: authentication, authorization, admission control, the actual etcd write, and finally a response, each a genuine, distinct stage, not an informal grouping.

blocks.alt: Five distinct, ordered stages, every single request passes through all of them

blocks.content: The first stage establishes identity, verifying who, or what, is actually making this request, a human user, or a ServiceAccount, covered in the Security module.

blocks.alt: Identity established first, before anything else even matters

blocks.content: This is exactly the RBAC system covered in complete depth in the Security module, checking whether the now-established identity actually has permission for this specific action, on this specific resource.

blocks.alt: The exact RBAC system from the Security module, applied at this precise stage

blocks.content: This is the genuine, specific detail worth knowing precisely, admission control itself runs in two ordered sub-phases: mutating admission (which can actually modify the request) runs first, then validating admission (which can only accept or reject, never modify) runs second, on the already-mutated result.

blocks.alt: Mutation first, then validation, on the already-mutated result, in that specific order

blocks.content: This is exactly the mechanism behind a service mesh automatically injecting a sidecar proxy, covered in the Sidecar Containers topic, a mutating admission webhook intercepts the Pod creation request and adds the sidecar container definition automatically, before the object is ever actually persisted.

blocks.alt: The real mechanism behind automatic sidecar injection, covered earlier in this course

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Every request travels through five ordered stages: authentication, authorization, admission control, the etcd write, and a response.

Admission control specifically runs mutating admission first (can modify the request), then validating admission second (can only accept or reject), exactly the mechanism behind automatic sidecar injection.
